paragraphs: AffordBot addresses a detailed form of reasoning about physical environments: identifying the particular part an instruction refers to and determining how that part can move. The paper defines this task through three outputs for each relevant element: its location, its motion type, and its motion axis. This makes the prediction more specific than simply naming an object.

The framework connects 3D scene information to multimodal language models through rendered views. It produces images from around the scene and projects candidate 3D elements into those images, preserving their relationship to the underlying geometry. The model first chooses a viewpoint that is informative for the instruction, then reasons through locating the relevant element and inferring plausible motion.

On SceneFun3D, the authors report state-of-the-art performance and strong generalization using point clouds and multimodal language models. The findings support combining viewpoint selection with structured reasoning: the framework links an instruction to both an actionable location and a geometrically grounded description of interaction.
neurips-2025-affordbot-3d-fine-grained-e.tldr: AffordBot uses selected scene views and structured multimodal reasoning to locate actionable 3D elements and infer their motion.

paragraphs: This paper examines how independently trained vision networks develop similar internal representations. Its audit covers dozens of models and thousands of layer comparisons, extending the analysis across training and unfamiliar image distributions. The central question is how much agreement exists, what transformations reveal it, and when that agreement develops.

The authors compare flexible linear alignment, rotations and reflections, and methods that match individual units. Rotations and reflections align representations almost as effectively as flexible linear transformations. Unit matching performs less well but substantially exceeds chance, indicating that individual representational directions have some shared structure. Almost all eventual alignment appears within the first training epoch, before accuracy settles.

These timing results indicate that shared input statistics and architectural biases largely drive alignment, rather than only the final task solution. Under distribution shifts, early layers remain closely aligned while deeper layers separate more as the shift increases. The findings therefore distinguish early shared structure from deeper representations whose agreement depends more strongly on the input distribution.
neurips-2025-bridging-critical-gaps-in-c.tldr: A large vision-model audit finds that representational alignment emerges early and becomes more sensitive to distribution shifts in deeper layers.

paragraphs: Answering questions about tables requires a model to connect language with structured data and logical operations. The paper identifies a source of unreliable answers: language models can lean on word combinations learned during pretraining instead of reasoning from the table. Strong overall language capabilities therefore do not by themselves resolve this source of bias.

Causal Intervention TableQA, or CIT, represents the task using a structural causal graph. Within that formulation, token co-occurrence patterns act as confounders that can distort the relationship between the question and the answer. CIT applies front-door adjustment to guide the generation of question variants and the subsequent reasoning process, aiming to reduce the influence of those misleading patterns.

Experiments across multiple benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance, with consistent gains across different language models. These results support the usefulness of the causal formulation for mitigating bias in TableQA. The contribution is a way to organize question variation and reasoning around an explicit account of why familiar language patterns can interfere with faithful table use.
neurips-2025-causality-meets-the-table-d.tldr: CIT uses a causal formulation and front-door adjustment to reduce token co-occurrence bias in language-model table reasoning.

paragraphs: This paper studies copying the recommendation logic of a system whose internal model is unavailable. Such extraction can reveal weaknesses in protection of user preferences and proprietary knowledge. The authors focus on two obstacles in existing approaches: needing accessible member or surrogate data, and training a replacement model that overfits generated interactions.

Their method, DBGRME, combines an interaction generator with a graph convolution-based surrogate. The generator addresses the absence of the data that extraction methods commonly assume is available. The surrogate is designed to capture varied and complex interaction patterns while improving generalization. This choice follows an analysis showing that the architecture of the replacement model substantially affects extraction performance.

Across several datasets and target models, the authors report stronger extraction in data-free settings. One stated example is a 17.4% improvement over the data-requiring PTQ method on LightGCN. The findings show that access to existing interaction data is not required for the reported attack performance, and that surrogate architecture is an important part of assessing extraction risk.
neurips-2025-data-free-model-extraction-.tldr: DBGRME combines generated interactions and a graph convolution surrogate to extract black-box recommender behavior without accessible interaction data.

paragraphs: Sparse autoencoders try to expose interpretable language-model features while keeping relatively few features active. Some learned features nevertheless activate frequently, prompting concern that they are artifacts of training. This paper investigates those dense features through their geometry, computational roles, and origins, finding that they often correspond to meaningful internal representations.

Dense features tend to appear in pairs pointing in opposite directions, together reconstructing particular directions in the model's residual stream. Removing their subspace reduces the appearance of new dense features when an autoencoder is retrained. That result suggests that frequent activation reflects properties of the underlying representation, rather than arising solely from the autoencoder training procedure.

The authors identify roles involving position, context binding, entropy regulation, letters, parts of speech, and principal components. They also find a progression across layers: structural features appear earlier, semantic features in the middle, and output-oriented features later. These findings argue against dismissing dense features merely because they violate an intuitive expectation of rarity; their frequency can accompany a functional role in computation.
neurips-2025-dense-sae-latents-are-featu.tldr: Frequently active sparse-autoencoder features often capture meaningful language-model computations rather than training noise.

paragraphs: Directed-Tokens addresses weaknesses in how large multimodal models connect visual information with text. Although these models perform well on many understanding tasks, their alignment between modalities can still limit robustness and generalization. The paper proposes teaching models to recover order from shuffled inputs as a way to improve that connection.

The method adds image-order and text-order reconstruction tasks during both pretraining and fine-tuning. It also introduces directed tokens that capture visual and textual knowledge and support reconstructing the correct order of visual inputs. An additional Image-to-Response Guided loss is intended to improve how the model's responses reflect visual understanding. These components place explicit training pressure on relationships among inputs and their connection to outputs.

The authors report consistent state-of-the-art performance relative to earlier multimodal models on task-oriented and instruction-following benchmarks. The stated findings support order reconstruction as a useful learning mechanism for reasoning, visual understanding, and cross-modal alignment. The approach matters because it adds concrete training tasks for improving these capabilities within the model's existing training phases.
neurips-2025-directed-tokens-a-robust-mu.tldr: Directed-Tokens trains multimodal models to reconstruct shuffled image and text order, improving alignment and benchmark performance.

paragraphs: In performative optimization, a decision can change the distribution of outcomes that the decision-maker faces. This creates a feedback problem: choosing well requires understanding how the environment responds. The paper addresses cases where that response is represented by an imperfect model, with scarce or costly data making misspecification especially consequential.

The proposed framework explicitly represents uncertainty about decision-dependent distributions through ambiguity sets. It introduces three modeling paradigms and an algorithm called repeated robust risk minimization. Each iteration solves a distributionally robust problem with the distributional dependence held separate, then updates the ambiguity set using the previous decision. This makes individual iterations tractable despite the nonconvex overall objective.

The authors provide formulations usable with existing solvers and theoretical guarantees concerning convergence and suboptimality. Numerical experiments in strategic classification, revenue management, and portfolio optimization show significant gains over state-of-the-art baselines. The contribution combines protection against an uncertain response model with an iterative procedure for handling decision feedback, connecting a difficult optimization formulation to practical computation.
neurips-2025-distributionally-robust-per.tldr: This framework optimizes decisions that reshape their own outcome distributions while accounting for uncertainty in that feedback.

paragraphs: SKETCH recognizes hand gestures by turning raw skeleton motion into visual graph representations. Earlier approaches often rely on selected measurements, such as joint distances, and dataset-specific preprocessing. The paper argues that these choices can discard spatial and temporal information while making recognition sensitive to changes in sensors, viewpoints, and body proportions.

The framework directly processes sequences containing time and three spatial coordinates. A learned Dynamic Range Embedding retains motion magnitudes along each axis that normalization and graph conversion would otherwise lose. It also normalizes each fixed-length time window independently during real-time processing, reducing sensitivity to fluctuations in absolute coordinates. The resulting graph images provide visual attention cues and can use pretrained vision backbones.

The authors describe the approach as independent of particular skeleton topologies, avoiding reliance on dataset- or sensor-specific definitions. On SHREC’19 and SHREC’22, they report better recognition robustness and generalization than state-of-the-art methods, alongside efficient convergence. The result supports visualizing raw motion as a useful representation, provided that the conversion preserves information about the scale of movement.
neurips-2025-doodle-to-detect-a-goofy-bu.tldr: SKETCH turns raw hand-skeleton sequences into graph images while preserving motion magnitudes to improve gesture recognition.

paragraphs: This paper tackles the tension between making neural networks smaller and keeping them resistant to adversarial inputs. Resource-constrained deployment benefits from compression, but the abstract identifies a recurring conflict with robustness. The proposed method aims to reduce model size while retaining accuracy on ordinary inputs and improving behavior under adversarial perturbations.

The approach uses dynamical low-rank training, enhanced by a spectral regularizer. That regularizer controls the condition number of each layer's low-rank core, targeting sensitivity within the compressed representation. The method also adapts ranks automatically, allowing the amount of compression to change with the network. The authors describe it as computationally efficient and applicable across models and data.

Experiments span standard architectures, datasets, and attacks. The reported networks achieve substantial compression while recovering or improving adversarial accuracy relative to uncompressed baselines, without sacrificing clean accuracy. The findings support incorporating robustness considerations directly into low-rank training. The important result is the observed combination of compactness and resistance to perturbations within the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-dynamical-low-rank-compress.tldr: Dynamical low-rank training with spectral regularization compresses networks while retaining clean accuracy and recovering or improving adversarial accuracy.

paragraphs: Estimating what happens after an intervention requires reasoning about causal relationships. Observational data can support several different causal graphs, so selecting just one can produce unjustified confidence. Bayesian inference addresses this by averaging over possible structures and mechanisms, but the rapidly growing number of graphs makes that calculation difficult.

MACE-TNP uses meta-learning to approximate this Bayesian calculation with an end-to-end model. Its training target is the model-averaged posterior distribution of intervention outcomes. The aim is therefore to predict an uncertainty-aware distribution that reflects multiple possible causal explanations, rather than first committing to one graph. Once learned, this mapping bypasses the expensive calculations otherwise needed for model averaging.

The authors report that MACE-TNP empirically outperforms strong Bayesian baselines. They present meta-learning as a flexible and scalable approach to approximating complex causal inference, with more challenging settings left as a direction for future scaling. The contribution matters because it treats uncertainty about causal structure as part of the prediction problem while pursuing a more computationally practical approximation.
neurips-2025-estimating-interventional-d.tldr: MACE-TNP learns to approximate Bayesian intervention predictions that average over uncertain causal structures and mechanisms.

paragraphs: FedRW addresses duplicated training samples in federated language-model training. Conventional deduplication can depend on a trusted third party and delete informative samples along with redundant ones. The paper instead proposes soft deduplication: retaining samples while adjusting their influence on learning, without assuming a trusted party to coordinate deletion.

The framework uses secure multi-party computation to implement frequency-aware reweighting. Global sample frequencies inform an adaptive mechanism that changes each sample's contribution to the training loss. Parallel orchestration is used to make the preprocessing efficient and scalable. These components connect privacy-preserving coordination with a training objective that accounts for repetition across the participating data.

The authors report improved generalization and robustness, enhanced security guarantees, and gains over a state-of-the-art method. The stated results include up to 28.78 times faster preprocessing and approximately 11.42% improvement in perplexity. The contribution shows how handling duplicates through their training weights can address both the cost of federated preprocessing and the risk of losing useful information through uniform deletion.
neurips-2025-fedrw-efficient-privacy-pre.tldr: FedRW securely reweights duplicated samples in federated language-model training, improving efficiency and perplexity without a trusted third party.

paragraphs: GOATex generates textures for both the outside and hidden inside surfaces of 3D meshes. The paper identifies a weakness in existing methods: good results on visible regions can coexist with missing interior textures and visible seams. Its approach explicitly organizes surfaces according to how deeply they are occluded.

The method uses rays cast from multiple views to assign mesh faces to ordered visibility layers, described through hit levels. A two-stage visibility strategy progressively exposes interior regions while preserving structural coherence. Each layer is textured using a pretrained diffusion model. A soft blending procedure then combines the textures in UV space, weighting contributions according to confidence in their visibility from different views.

Empirical results show consistent improvements over existing methods, including seamless, high-fidelity textures on visible and occluded surfaces. GOATex does not require fine-tuning the diffusion model and allows separate prompts for exterior and interior regions. This gives the user control over different layers of appearance while the visibility-aware processing addresses surfaces that ordinary exterior views leave hidden.
neurips-2025-goatex-geometry-occlusion-a.tldr: GOATex textures visible and hidden mesh surfaces by revealing visibility layers and blending diffusion-generated textures.

paragraphs: HouseLayout3D addresses the gap between estimating layouts in simple synthetic scenes and handling real buildings with multiple floors. The paper argues that existing training datasets emphasize uncomplicated, single-floor spaces. As a result, models struggle with larger architectural structures, and processing one floor at a time loses information about the building as a whole.

The authors introduce a real-world benchmark designed to expose these weaknesses in expansive and architecturally complex spaces. They also propose MultiFloor3D, a baseline that combines advances in 3D reconstruction and 2D segmentation. This connects methods for recovering spatial structure with methods for dividing images into meaningful regions, providing an approach to layout estimation without layout-specific training.

MultiFloor3D significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on both the new benchmark and existing datasets, according to the reported results. The contribution therefore has two parts: a more demanding evaluation setting and a strong baseline for it. Together, they highlight the importance of preserving building-wide context and demonstrate useful performance without a dedicated layout-training stage.
neurips-2025-houselayout3d-a-benchmark-a.tldr: HouseLayout3D benchmarks complex real buildings, while MultiFloor3D improves layout estimation without layout-specific training.

paragraphs: Synthetic images are useful for training only if their quality and diversity suit the real data a model will encounter. This paper argues that improved visual quality can come with reduced diversity, and that guidance methods may overlook differences between generated and real distributions. Chamfer Guidance uses a small set of real examples to address both concerns.

The method guides generation without additional training, using those examples to characterize desirable quality and coverage. On ImageNet-1k and geographic diversity benchmarks, it increases diversity relative to real-image datasets while maintaining or improving quality. With two real examples, the reported precision and distributional coverage are 96.4% and 86.4%; with 32, they reach 97.5% and 92.7%.

Classifiers trained on its synthetic images gain up to 15% in-distribution accuracy and up to 16% out-of-distribution accuracy over the baselines. Sampling also uses 31% fewer FLOPs than classifier-free-guidance approaches because no unconditional model is required. These findings connect improved generation coverage to downstream learning utility, alongside a reduction in sampling computation.
neurips-2025-increasing-the-utility-of-s.tldr: Chamfer Guidance uses a few real examples to improve synthetic-image diversity, downstream classifier accuracy, and sampling efficiency.

paragraphs: LaM-SLidE brings latent-space generation to systems made of interacting entities, such as molecules or groups of people. Compressing these systems into a latent representation creates a particular challenge: the model must still track individual entities over time and retain information about their composition and connections. Efficient generation alone does not address that requirement.

The approach introduces identifier representations that link entities to the compressed system state. These identifiers allow retrieval of entity properties and composition from the latent representation, supporting traceability. With that link in place, the method uses pretrained encoders and decoders to carry out generative modeling directly in latent space, following a pattern used successfully in image and video generation.

Experiments across different domains report favorable speed, accuracy, and generalizability. The contribution is the connection between efficient latent modeling and explicit access to the entities being modeled. It shows a way to use a compressed system representation while retaining the ability to recover information about its individual components throughout a generated trajectory.
neurips-2025-lam-slide-latent-space-mode.tldr: LaM-SLidE uses entity identifiers to preserve traceability while generating dynamical-system trajectories in latent space.

paragraphs: This paper separates two aspects of language-model safety: judging an instruction as harmful and deciding to refuse it. The authors identify an internal harmfulness direction distinct from the previously studied refusal direction. Their question is whether a model's assessment of harmfulness can remain intact even when its refusal behavior changes.

Steering along the harmfulness direction can make a model interpret harmless instructions as harmful. Steering along the refusal direction instead tends to produce refusals without reversing the harmfulness judgment. The authors also find that certain jailbreaks weaken refusal signals while leaving the internal harmfulness belief present, and that adversarial fine-tuning to accept harmful instructions has minimal effect on that belief.

The resulting Latent Guard uses the internal harmfulness representation to detect unsafe inputs and reduce over-refusals. Across different jailbreak methods, it performs comparably to or better than Llama Guard 3 8B and is reported to resist fine-tuning attacks. These findings suggest that internal harmfulness judgments can provide a more robust safety signal than the model's outward refusal decision.
neurips-2025-llms-encode-harmfulness-and.tldr: Language models can retain an internal harmfulness judgment even when refusal is weakened, enabling an internal safety detector.

paragraphs: MPMAvatar builds human avatars from multi-view videos, focusing on the difficult dynamics of loose clothing. An avatar must capture how garments deform and contact the body while also rendering convincingly from different viewpoints. The paper addresses limitations in the accuracy of existing physical simulations and their robustness to new animation inputs.

Its central component is a Material Point Method simulator adapted for garments. The simulator includes an anisotropic constitutive model, allowing material behavior to depend on direction, and a new collision-handling algorithm for contact with the body. This dynamics model is combined with a canonical avatar rendered through 3D Gaussian Splatting and quasi-shadowing, connecting physical motion to high-fidelity appearance.

The experiments report significant improvements over the existing state-of-the-art physics-based avatar in dynamics accuracy, rendering accuracy, robustness, and efficiency. The authors also demonstrate an application involving unseen interactions without additional training. That result illustrates the value of the simulator's generalization: the avatar can handle interaction conditions beyond those demonstrated during learning in the reported application.
neurips-2025-mpmavatar-learning-3d-gauss.tldr: MPMAvatar combines tailored garment physics with Gaussian rendering to produce accurate, robust human-avatar animations.

paragraphs: Offline safe reinforcement learning aims to learn a high-reward policy from a fixed dataset while respecting a cumulative cost budget. The challenge is to optimize performance and enforce that constraint using the available data. This paper proposes a method that combines offline reinforcement learning with online optimization inside the learning procedure.

The authors express the problem as a minimax objective and solve it by combining the two types of algorithms. They prove approximate optimality when the approach uses an approximate offline reinforcement-learning oracle and no-regret online optimization. The guarantee is therefore tied to those components. The use of online optimization concerns the optimization process, while the policy-learning problem remains based on fixed data.

A practical approximation can be paired with any offline reinforcement-learning algorithm and removes the need for offline policy evaluation. On the DSRL benchmark, the method reliably satisfies safety constraints under stringent cost budgets while obtaining high rewards. The contribution links a theoretically supported formulation with a practical route for adding cost-constrained learning to existing offline methods.
neurips-2025-online-optimization-for-off.tldr: This method combines offline reinforcement learning and online optimization to learn high-reward policies under cumulative cost constraints.

paragraphs: PreFM addresses recognizing audio, visual, and combined audio-visual events as a video stream arrives. The paper introduces Online Audio-Visual Event Parsing to distinguish this setting from methods that process a complete video. Streaming creates two linked demands: interpreting events from limited context and keeping the model efficient enough for real-time use.

The framework predicts future multimodal cues and incorporates useful predictions into its current understanding. This supplies additional inferred context when the incoming evidence is ambiguous. It also learns robust representations that are not tied to a particular modality and uses focal temporal prioritization to improve precision and generalization. These components jointly address uncertainty about events and the selective use of temporal information.

On UnAV-100 and LLP, the authors report large improvements over state-of-the-art methods with significantly fewer parameters. The results support predictive future modeling as a way to improve online event interpretation while reducing model size. Its future information is inferred within the framework, allowing the task to remain centered on sequentially arriving video.
neurips-2025-prefm-online-audio-visual-e.tldr: PreFM predicts useful future audio-visual cues to improve streaming event recognition with fewer model parameters.

paragraphs: ResearchCodeBench evaluates whether language models can turn new machine-learning research ideas into executable implementations. The paper focuses on contributions unseen during pretraining, where reproducing familiar code does not resolve the task. This targets a specific research capability: understanding a paper's contribution well enough to express it faithfully in code.

The benchmark draws on leading research papers from 2024–2025 and evaluates more than 30 proprietary and open-source language models. Its scope connects recent research contributions with implementation tasks, making code generation a test of applying novel ideas. The authors also examine performance differences, contamination, and error patterns, treating the evaluation as more than a single aggregate score.

Even the strongest evaluated models correctly implement less than 40% of the code, according to the reported finding. This indicates substantial remaining difficulty on the benchmark despite broader progress in language-model coding. The platform is intended to support continued measurement and improvement of research implementation, giving this particular form of model-assisted innovation a dedicated evaluation setting.
neurips-2025-researchcodebench-benchmark.tldr: ResearchCodeBench finds that even leading evaluated language models correctly implement less than 40% of novel research code.

paragraphs: Boosting turns weak learning procedures into stronger predictors. This paper studies its sample requirements in the agnostic setting, where no assumptions are made about the distribution of labels. That setting broadens the problem beyond the realizable case and leaves the statistical cost of weak-to-strong learning less fully understood.

The authors propose an algorithm with substantially improved sample complexity under very general assumptions. Their construction first reduces the problem to the realizable case, then uses margin-based filtering to select high-quality hypotheses. The approach therefore combines a connection to a better-studied learning setting with a filtering step that identifies useful candidate predictors.

The paper also proves a lower bound that nearly matches the algorithm's sample requirement. Together, the algorithm and lower bound settle agnostic boosting's sample complexity up to logarithmic factors. This is a statement about how much data the learning problem requires: the proposed upper bound approaches a fundamental lower limit. The remaining logarithmic gap preserves the distinction between a nearly tight characterization and an exact match.
neurips-2025-revisiting-agnostic-boostin.tldr: A new agnostic boosting algorithm and nearly matching lower bound characterize sample complexity up to logarithmic factors.

paragraphs: ROVER helps vision-language models reason about long videos of embodied tasks. Understanding individual images does not automatically translate into tracking an extended task attempt. The framework recursively divides a trajectory into shorter segments associated with subtasks, allowing reasoning to focus on local frame sequences while retaining the larger task context.

The implementation uses in-context learning and is evaluated on OpenX Embodiment videos and a new RoboCasa-derived dataset. The latter contains 543 videos across 27 manipulation tasks, including expert trajectories and perturbed non-expert behavior. ROVER exceeds strong baselines in estimating task progress, producing frame-level natural-language reasoning, and answering questions about videos.

The authors observe fewer hallucinations when the model reasons over fewer frames at each step, especially during unexpected or non-optimal behavior. A sliding context window specific to the current subtask also gives linear time complexity in video length, an asymptotic improvement over the baselines. The findings connect task decomposition to both more accurate interpretation and more efficient processing of extended visual sequences.
neurips-2025-rover-recursive-reasoning-o.tldr: ROVER recursively splits task videos into subtasks, improving reasoning and reducing hallucinations with linear scaling in video length.

paragraphs: SceneWeaver generates indoor 3D environments through an agent that repeatedly evaluates and revises its work. The paper targets several weaknesses in existing scene generation: restricted room categories, insufficient object detail, physical inconsistencies, and difficulty following complex instructions. These issues matter for embodied AI, where environments need useful structure as well as convincing appearance.

A language-model planner chooses among an extensible collection of generation tools, including data-driven, visual, and language-model-based methods. It evaluates the scene for physical plausibility, visual realism, and agreement with the user's request. When it identifies a semantic inconsistency, it can select a targeted tool and update the environment, repeating this process across successive iterations.

Experiments cover both common room types and open-vocabulary categories. The authors report improvements over prior methods on physical, visual, and semantic metrics, together with effective generalization to complex scenes and varied instructions. The contribution is a unified refinement process that coordinates different generation methods and uses self-evaluation to guide concrete changes to the resulting environment.
neurips-2025-sceneweaver-all-in-one-3d-s.tldr: SceneWeaver coordinates scene-generation tools through repeated planning and self-evaluation to improve 3D environments and instruction alignment.

paragraphs: RICE addresses inefficient reasoning in mixture-of-experts language models, including spending too much or too little effort on a problem. These models selectively activate different experts during computation. The paper proposes steering that activation at inference time to improve reasoning depth and efficiency without additional training or complex heuristics.

The method uses normalized Pointwise Mutual Information to identify specialized experts associated with meta-level reasoning operations. It then reinforces these cognitive experts during inference. This links the steering mechanism to identifiable internal components of the model, providing a concrete target for adjusting reasoning behavior while leaving the intervention lightweight.

Evaluations use DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3-235B on AIME and GPQA Diamond. The authors report consistent improvements in reasoning accuracy, cognitive efficiency, and cross-domain generalization, while preserving general instruction-following skills. They also report substantial gains over steering through prompts and decoding constraints. The findings support reinforcing specialized experts as a practical and interpretable way to influence reasoning effort in the evaluated mixture-of-experts models.
neurips-2025-two-experts-are-all-you-nee.tldr: RICE reinforces identified cognitive experts at inference time to improve mixture-of-experts reasoning accuracy and efficiency without retraining.

paragraphs: Gait-World explores how human vocabulary can help describe and recognize walking patterns. Existing gait networks use appearance, motion, or structural information, but those learned concepts can be difficult for people to interpret. The paper selects actions within a gait cycle as a vocabulary base, aiming to connect gait representations with understandable language.

Its first model, α-Gait, uses vocabulary knowledge from vision-language models to guide a gait network. Directly combining the two sources is difficult because vocabulary and gait features occupy different representation spaces. A Vocabulary Relation Mapper and Gait Fine-grained Detector establish vocabulary relations within the gait space and detect the corresponding gait features.

Experiments on CASIA-B, CCPG, SUSTech1K, Gait3D, and GREW reveal potential value in bringing vocabulary information into gait recognition. The stated conclusion emphasizes that potential and the research directions it opens. The approach matters because it offers both a source of guidance beyond limited gait datasets and a route toward connecting learned walking features with concepts people can name.
neurips-2025-vocabulary-guided-gait-reco.tldr: Gait-World uses vocabulary about gait-cycle actions to guide gait feature learning and connect walking representations with human concepts.
